s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with dysarthria, dysphagia, and cognitive impairment
salient_findings: Progressive dysarthria and dysphagia over 6 months
Vertical gaze palsy and tongue atrophy
Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia on 11C-CFT PET imaging
key_facts: 48-year-old woman
6-month history of progressive dysarthria and dysphagia
Family history of relative with memory problems after age 80
Cognitive impairment on neurological examination
Vertical gaze palsy on neurological examination
Tongue atrophy on neurological examination
Pyramidal signs on neurological examination
Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia on 11C-CFT PET imaging
Almost total loss of dopamine transporter binding in caudate nucleus
Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene (p.E643del) identified by whole-exon sequencing
Autoimmune encephalitis antibodies negative in serum and CSF

shortlist.label: TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia
shortlist.why_kept: Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene identified

shortlist.label: Progressive supranuclear palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Vertical gaze palsy and severe loss of dopamine transporter binding

shortlist.label: Frontotemporal dementia
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive dysarthria, dysphagia, and cognitive impairment

shortlist.label: Corticobasal degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Combination of cognitive, motor, and speech symptoms

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene (p.E643del) and the combination of cognitive impairment, vertical gaze palsy, tongue atrophy, and pyramidal signs are consistent with TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia.

rejected.label: Progressive supranuclear palsy
rejected.why: While vertical gaze palsy is a feature of progressive supranuclear palsy, the genetic finding of a TBK1 pathogenic variant and the overall clinical presentation better support TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia.

rejected.label: Frontotemporal dementia
rejected.why: Frontotemporal dementia is a broader category, and the specific genetic finding of a TBK1 pathogenic variant points towards TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia as the more precise diagnosis.

rejected.label: Corticobasal degeneration
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and genetic findings do not specifically align with corticobasal degeneration, which typically involves more asymmetric motor features and alien limb syndrome, not prominently featured in this case.

rejected.label: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
rejected.why: While tongue atrophy and pyramidal signs could suggest amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, the presence of cognitive impairment, vertical gaze palsy, and the specific genetic mutation points away from this diagnosis.
